title: Shared-index staging discipline is insufficient under concurrent agents; deployment and publishing work uses one isolated git worktree per task
notes: Two Claude sessions share one working tree on this machine. Three times on 2026-09-02 a concurrent session's `git add` of its own paths also swept in another session's uncommitted edits to files it had touched, because the index is shared state and an edit in the working tree carries no ownership.

Recurrence 1 -- commit 29ed345 ('docs: seal JaxFNE visual theme ... and update README skills documentation') swept an in-progress README.md edit. The committed README then referenced examples/quickstart_jnwb.py and examples/figures/jnwb_quickstart.png, neither of which was tracked, so on a fresh clone the image did not render and the documented command failed. Repaired by 8ca5567.

Recurrence 2 -- commit 9211b31 ('harness: strengthen root freeze, symbol docs & dataset gates, add guide 11 and quickstart example') swept in the AGENTS.md 4.3 amendment that was written specifically to prohibit this. The rule's own first commit is an instance of the failure it prohibits. No repair needed: the amendment text landed byte-identical.

Recurrence 3 -- commit 2af5f86 ('docs: add artifacts/AGENTS.md policy reference, docs link in README, and strengthen root freeze') swept in a .gitignore block and a docs/index.md toctree entry for docs/12_interactive_analyses.md, WITHOUT the document, which was still untracked. This was the most costly of the three: it broke the committed tree.

Recurrence 3 receipt -- `git archive HEAD` into a temp dir, then `python -m sphinx -W -b html docs docs/_build/html` produced: "WARNING: toctree contains reference to nonexisting document '12_interactive_analyses' [toc.not_readable]" and "build finished with problems, 1 warning (with warnings treated as errors)". This fails the CI docs gate (.github/workflows/workflow.yml:74) and Read the Docs (.readthedocs.yaml sets fail_on_warning: true). Repaired by d94532d, which commits the missing document; the same command on the new HEAD returns "build succeeded".

DECIDED 2026-09-02 by Hamm: one writable git worktree per concurrent agent or task, rather than further prose in AGENTS.md. The rule that was added (AGENTS.md 4.3: no `git commit -a`, and inspect `git diff --cached --name-only` before every commit) stays in force -- it is correct and cheap -- but it binds only a session that is already behaving correctly, so it cannot be the primary control.

EVIDENCE FOR, measured rather than argued. Shared working tree: three staging collisions in one day (29ed345, 9211b31, 2af5f86), one of which broke `sphinx -W` on main and was recorded as a CI failure. Isolated worktrees: three subsequent operations with zero collisions -- the gh-pages deployment (6d05244), the Analysis 6A terminology pass (f417e93 / efe3728), and the main-into-dev reconciliation -- each run while a concurrent session was committing to the shared tree on a different branch.

WHY IT WORKS: the failing property is 'were these edits authored by the session committing them', which is not expressible as a check the committing session can run, because the index is shared state. A per-task worktree removes the shared index instead of policing it.

COST, so the decision is not oversold: a fresh worktree lacks every git-ignored input. The terminology pass needed three copied in by hand before it could build -- the frozen figure SVGs, onset6a_corpus_census.csv, and the private identifier map. The visibility gate failed closed on the missing identifier map, which is the correct behaviour but is a step a deployment runbook must state explicitly.

PRECEDENT TO FOLLOW: `omission/atlas/deploy_ghpages.py` refuses to run from the shared working tree and verifies the site fingerprint on both sides of the copy. Publishing steps should keep that shape.
issues: The AGENTS.md 4.3 amendment (git commit -a prohibition + mandatory `git diff --cached --name-only` inspection) is correct and necessary, but it is prose addressed to a session that is behaving correctly. It cannot bind a concurrent session that stages first, and it did not prevent recurrences 2 and 3.

scripts/harness_gate.py::check_protected_paths is the only mechanical staging gate. It guards a fixed protected-path list (README.md, .gitignore, docs/index.md are not on it) and runs in CI, after the push, so it cannot catch this class.
The failing property is not 'which paths were staged' but 'were these edits authored by the session that is committing them', which no rule expressible in prose can check.

OPEN, found 2026-09-02 while acting on this decision: scripts/harness_gate.py is not worktree-aware. Its repository-root allowlist rejects `.git` when that is a FILE, which is exactly what a linked worktree has (`gitdir: ...`) instead of a directory. Running the gate inside a worktree therefore fails with UNAUTHORIZED_ROOT_FILE, and tests/test_harness_adversarial_gates.py::test_real_repository_passes_all_harness_gates fails with it. Verified as an artifact, not a real violation: the same gate returns ALL HARNESS GATES PASSED on a normal checkout and on a `git archive` export of the same commit. Now that worktrees are the standard for deployment and publishing work, this will fire routinely. Not fixed here -- recorded as debt, since repository maintenance is closed for this phase.

verification.method: direct inspection of the committed trees plus a Sphinx build of `git archive HEAD` in an isolated temp directory
verification.confirmed_by: the CI docs gate and Read the Docs both enforce the exact condition that recurrence 3 violated, and the breakage was reproduced from the committed tree; separately, three isolated-worktree operations completed with zero collisions under the same concurrency
